nature: Exploratory retrospective pilot, specified before these ranking calculations but after viewing the original study; not confirmatory or preregistered
question: At the same grade-specific inspection allocations, do frozen complete-model scores identify more hazardous records than random within-grade ranking?
cohorts: The four existing record-order test blocks, separately and pooled without crossing boundaries; no holdout
score_source: Saved Stage 2 fixed XGBoost test scores; no fitting, retuning, calibration or threshold reselection
capacity: K=floor(budget*N) in each phase; pooled totals sum phase-specific K and never rerank across phases
methods: Grade priority with uniform random selection within the boundary grade, evaluated analytically
Grade priority then decreasing frozen XGBoost score
Global decreasing frozen XGBoost score, auxiliary
primary_contrast: Observed grade-first ML detections minus analytic expected grade-random detections; both use identical grade-specific allocations and total K
secondary_contrast: Global ML detections minus grade-random expectation; this can change allocations across grades and does not isolate within-grade information
ties: A prespecified label-independent uniform key per original test row breaks equal ML scores; grade-first and global methods share keys. Duplicate bootstrap copies retain the original key and label, so their relative order cannot affect detection totals.
tie_seed_rule: tie_seed+fold+1, generated in increasing original row order separately within each phase
random_reference: Each grade receives k_g slots. E[TP_random]=sum(k_g*P_g/N_g). Save the exact conditional allocation distribution by convolving hypergeometric grade distributions; its percentile range is allocation randomness on the fixed queue, not a generalization confidence interval.
resampling: Within-phase moving-block draws. Reconstruct each sampled queue, recompute grade allocations, rerank both ML methods at the same K, and recompute the analytic random expectation. Keep all zero-positive draws. Use identical sampled records for every method and budget.
interval_scope: Unadjusted percentile intervals for frozen-score batch-ranking contrasts on these record-order queues; excludes fitting, feature selection and tuning uncertainty
loss_identity: At fixed P and K, L=r*P+K-(r+1)*TP; ranking loss differences follow directly from detection differences and are not independent outcomes. No extra cost grid is run.
interpretation: Full scores also use other grades and shift type. Any increment concerns the full score, not an isolated monitoring/sensor effect. Matched information-source models require a separate future protocol. Records are not verified simultaneous inspection candidates, so this is not real-time dispatch validation.
no_test_selection: Retain every phase and budget regardless of direction; do not choose a winning budget, grade, model or tie seed from test outcomes
